papers.abstract: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to follow a language-specified person under occlusion, look-alike distractors, and ambiguous instructions. We show that improving tracking persistence can simultaneously increase safety violations. Using a compact 0.6B vision-language-action (VLA) tracker with a frozen backbone, we update only the planner head with proximal policy optimization (PPO). PPO improves success and following rates across all three EVT-Bench settings, but increases the collision rate on distracted tracking because episodes that previously ended in target loss can instead end in contact. We introduce TRACE, an execution-time target-state risk gate that preserves the learned policy and intervenes selectively. A lightweight risk head processes 84 cues, including candidate boxes, identity margins, a learned range-and-bearing probe, and the policy's commands. When the calibrated risk exceeds a threshold, TRACE rescales the translational component of the next waypoint while leaving yaw unchanged. The executed action is identical to PPO's on more than 98% of steps. In paired evaluations on identical episodes, TRACE reduces the distracted-tracking collision rate by 3.96 percentage points, while further improving success and following rates. Matched slowdown controls without target-state timing do not reproduce this improvement. Concurrent evaluation reproduces a collision reduction of 3.77 points, compared with 0.29 points for identical-arm null pairs, indicating that the effect exceeds evaluation variability. These results show that target-state-aware execution can recover the safety cost of policy post-training with minimal intervention.

analysis.key_results: TRACE在EVT-Bench三个设置上提高了成功率和跟随率；在分散注意力的跟踪中碰撞率降低3.96个百分点（并发评估为3.77个百分点），且在超过98%的步骤上与PPO策略执行动作相同。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出TRACE，一种执行时目标状态风险门控机制，通过选择性干预从PPO训练得到的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）跟踪器输出，在保持追踪性能的同时降低碰撞率。
analysis.method: 在0.6B参数VLA跟踪器上使用PPO仅更新规划器头；TRACE利用轻量风险头处理84个线索（候选框、身份边界、学习到的距离方位探针、策略命令等），当校准风险超过阈值时，仅缩放下一航点的平移分量，偏航角不变。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 该文提出TRACE，一种在测试时根据目标状态风险干预VLA策略执行的方法，以减少具身跟踪中的碰撞同时保持追踪性能。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 本文直接聚焦于VLA（视觉-语言-动作）模型在具身跟踪任务中的安全执行问题，提出一种与模型无关的执行时干预机制，以缓解策略后训练带来的安全代价，对VLA在真实机器人部署中的安全性有直接价值。

papers.abstract: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. We then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery, and distill a small student that replaces the teacher in the same harness. On RoboTwin, harness evolution raises the teacher's success from 33.4% to 63.6%; the final 4B student reaches 62.8%. Across four harness versions, distilled 4B students score close to their corresponding teachers, and later versions yield stronger students, showing that harness evolution gains carry into compact models. The harness gains also transfer to other frozen planners without retraining. On identical episodes, the final 4B student outperforms open 4B agents, the open 27B harness-RSI model SenseNova-RoboRSI, and our own teacher model placed in three competitors' harnesses. It stays close to its teacher on all three training benchmarks, and on three benchmarks never used for RSI or training it scores close to a 552B planner running the same harness. On the measured deployment episodes, it uses about one fifth of its teacher's accelerator time.

analysis.key_results: 在RoboTwin上，harness进化将教师成功率从33.4%提升至63.6%，最终4B学生模型达到62.8%；在相同部署片段上，4B学生的加速器耗时约为教师的五分之一，并在多个基准上接近其教师，超越多个基线。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出两阶段方法TinyAstral：先通过递归自改进（RSI）提升冻结教师模型的harness，再蒸馏出在相同harness中运行的小型学生模型，实现高性能低成本的机器人操作智能体。
analysis.method: 第一阶段，冻结教师模型，通过递归自改进让前沿LLM代理分析教师轨迹并提议harness编辑，仅接受通过配对统计检验的编辑；第二阶段，冻结最终harness，收集教师轨迹并进行蒸馏，训练小规模学生模型替换教师。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出TinyAstral，通过递归自改进教师模型的环境并蒸馏出小型学生模型，在保持规划能力的同时大幅降低推理成本。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 本文直接面向视觉-语言驱动的机器人操作智能体（VLA），通过harness改进和知识蒸馏，在保持规划能力的同时显著降低推理成本，对VLA的高效部署和小型化具有直接借鉴意义。

(a) With teacher weights frozen, RSI improves the harness; we then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories, and distill small students. (b) Harness evolution improves the teacher and other frozen planners. Students trained separately at four harness versions each approach their corresponding teacher. figures.caption: Overview of TinyAstral. Stage 1: humans specify the rules and budget in advance. A master of frontier LLM agents reads trajectories of the frozen teacher acting through the harness (tools, feedback, memory, recovery) and proposes harness edits, which are accepted only if a paired A/B test on selection seeds passes a pre-registered statistical gate; model weights never change. Stage 2: after evolution ends, we freeze H ∗ H^{*} and collect teacher trajectories, including reasoning and recovery branches. These are mixed with offline real-robot supervision to train tiny students (0.8B–4B), which replace the teacher in the same harness. Evaluation covers three training domains and three unseen benchmarks, plus three closed-loop real-robot tasks on an SO-ARM101 arm.
figures.label: Figure 2

papers.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
papers.title_zh: TinyAstral：将自进化规划器环境迁移到小型通用操作智能体

papers.abstract: LLM agents execute tasks through repeated model calls over evolving histories of reasoning, actions, and tool feedback. Aggregate speculative-decoding metrics merge these distinct decisions, providing limited guidance on where draft supervision is needed. We present TraceSpec, a framework connecting trajectory evaluation with adaptive draft training. It combines dynamic execution with fixed-prefix replay and introduces TraceSpec-Traj, a corpus of 10,000 training states and 2,500 test states spanning browsing and software engineering. Analysis of five speculative baselines reveals that aggregate acceptance can rise with context length while declining within matched late browsing actions. Workload and phase further distinguish these trends, motivating supervision guided by trajectory conditions. TraceSpec trains on intermediate assistant turns and allocates a fixed prediction budget using state-conditioned estimates of prefix-aware acceptance gaps. Across three target sizes and two temperatures, it improves replay throughput by 12.5% to 22.6% over its DSpark base. Qwen3-4B ablations show that adaptive allocation increases accepted length by 3.3% to 10.0% over fixed full-turn supervision, with additional comparisons substantiating the roles of state conditioning and consecutive-token agreement. The resulting evaluation resources, trajectory findings, and training strategy connect the analysis of agent execution to practical draft improvement.

analysis.key_results: 在三个目标规模和两个温度下，回放吞吐量比DSpark基线提高12.5%至22.6%；Qwen3-4B消融显示自适应分配使接受长度比固定全轮监督提高3.3%至10.0%。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出TraceSpec框架，连接轨迹评估与自适应草稿训练，并构建TraceSpec-Traj数据集，分析智能体轨迹中的推测解码特征。
analysis.method: 结合动态执行与固定前缀回放，在中间助手轮次训练草稿模型，并根据状态条件估计的前缀感知接受度差距进行自适应预测预算分配。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出TraceSpec框架，通过轨迹评估和自适应草稿训练来提升LLM智能体的推测解码效率。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该工作专注于LLM智能体的推测解码效率，不涉及VLA、WAM或机器人动作-世界建模，但与本站效率推理主题间接相关，可为具身模型的高效推理提供方法参考。

figures.caption: TraceSpec overview. (a) Trajectory-state construction, coverage, and source-task splits. (b) Dynamic execution and fixed-prefix replay with trajectory diagnosis. (c) Full-turn supervision with state-conditioned allocation and event-normalized sampling under a fixed prediction budget. Three panels connect trajectory data, evaluation, and adaptive draft training. Panel a constructs history and continuation pairs across two workloads, five context strata, and four phases, with source tasks split into training and test partitions. Panel b shows dynamic draft verification by frozen Qwen3, tool feedback updating the history, and five baseline drafters evaluated on identical saved test prefixes. Trajectory diagnostics summarize acceptance, throughput, and episode latency. Panel c expands target-generated training trajectories into assistant segments. Frozen Qwen3 outputs and features supervise a trainable DSpark-based draft. Token overlap contributes to acceptance gaps smoothed by context, phase, workload, and tool state. Base coverage and adaptive priority determine supervision shares, converted to segment sampling probabilities using expected prediction events per visit. Training feedback updates allocation, and the resulting draft returns to evaluation.
